fences.text: (CHAR-03 再利用) A side-on view of a narrow mountain trail in a forest near Setana, southwestern Hokkaido, in early April early spring: bare deciduous trees, brown leaf litter, fresh green shoots of wild garlic, No snow anywhere, no frost, no ice, no winter. A Japanese woman in her mid 40s in a MAROON field jacket (deep red-brown, NOT green, NOT grey), charcoal trousers and dark hair tied low in a short bun walks from left to right across the frame, facing forward to the right, NOT turning around, NOT looking back, her face turned away from the camera and not identifiable, a small canvas bag on her shoulder. Behind her on the left, an adult male Hokkaido brown bear about 2 metres long and roughly 150 to 250 kilograms lunges out of the bamboo thicket ON ALL FOURS, NOT upright, NOT on two legs, head dropped low and driven forward, jaws wrenched wide open in a savage snarl with long fangs bared, ears pinned flat, the fur along its neck and spine bristled into a raised ridge, claws fully extended. Captured at the moment just before contact only, nothing beyond it. Framed side-on from adult eye height about eight metres away. Terrifying, sudden, cold muted tones. Photorealistic, shot on RED camera. Documentary style. 16:9 aspect ratio. Generate 1 image.
